title: Deadlock storm
summary: Pairs of sessions deadlock with each other round after round: in 'order' rounds side 1 locks inventory row A then B while side 2 locks B then A; in 'conversion' rounds both sides read row A with HOLDLOCK and then both update it. Side 2 runs at DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW, so it's the victim (error 1205). Every round rolls back, each victim is recorded as a deadlock-victim event, and each session stops after maxRounds rounds.

concurrency.description: Session pairs; each pair deadlocks with itself on its own two inventory rows (101 to 116), apart from locking-blocking's rows 1 and 2.

intensity.description: Pause between rounds: about 10 seconds at 1, 1 second at 10.

notes.T3: Row versioning doesn't prevent these deadlocks: both shapes take exclusive or HOLDLOCK shared locks. With optimized locking, the deadlock graph shows transaction-ID (xactlock) resources.

shape.description: order: two rows locked in opposite order. conversion: a shared lock (HOLDLOCK) that both sides try to convert to an update. mixed: alternate the two each round.

maxRounds.description: Rounds per session at most, so a run causes at most concurrency x maxRounds deadlocks.

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerPerformanceCountersCommon: Number of Deadlocks/sec above 0 (a cumulative counter: deltas per bin)
SqlServerWaitStats: Lock wait category (LCK_M_X, LCK_M_U) for the second of each pair until the deadlock monitor picks a victim
SqlServerPerformanceCountersCommon: Errors/sec rising with the 1205 errors
A deadlock finding with the two statements and a recommended access-order change that needs approval
expectedHubSignals.note: Preview; coverage by target is undocumented (ADR 0013).

expectedSymptoms: Repeated error 1205: one session of each pair is chosen as the deadlock victim every round
Short lock waits (up to the deadlock monitor's interval) before each victim is picked
Alternating deadlock shapes in the deadlock graphs: key locks in opposite order, and a shared-to-exclusive conversion on one key
queryLevelEvidence: demo.scenario_run_events: one deadlock-victim event per victim (pair, shape, round, session ID), 500 at most per run
The system_health session's xml_deadlock_report events on SQL Server (needs VIEW SERVER STATE)
reset: Every round rolls back, so the inventory rows stay as seeded. Reset stops the run and kills leftover ContosoCare.Demo/ sessions in this database only.
